newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 19.

text.p: PRAVO - Norway will supply natural gas to the Czech Republic, according to a decision made on Tuesday during a meeting of Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy and Norwiegan Trade Minister Grete Knudsen in Prague.
- Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy should present a proposal to the cabinet today for resolving the situation at Poldi Steel.
- Motoinvest Group decided to attempt to call a general shareholders meeting for Agrobanka to approve its decision to liquidate the bank, according to the director of Motoinvest, Jan Dienstl.
- The federation of businessmen in the Czech Republic want health insurance rates to drop one percentage point from the current 13.5 percent.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Within one week, the proposal for health reforms will be discussed in a meeting which Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus will call, according to Health Minister Jan Strasky.
- Norwegian King Harald V arrived yesterday in Prague with Queen Sonja for a three day vist at the invitation of President Vaclav Havel.
- The National Property Find sold 37 percent of shares of Medicamenta a.s. to BH Securities last week.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Although the chairman of the Social Democratic Party (CSSD) succeeded in definitively removing Jozef Wagner from CSSD, the battle is not over. Parliament refused to acknowledge CSSD's claim to Wagner's position as chairman of the budgetary committee.
- Taxi services will remain deregulated, ministers decided yesterday.
- Teachers are threatening to boycott the start of the next school year, the chairman of the school workers union, Jaroslav Rossler, said yesterday.
- 100 share issues will be delisted tomorrow because they do not fulfill criteria laid down by the stock exchange.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Another dispute has arisen between the owners of Poldi, Bohemia Art and state-owned Holding Kladno. Pro Win, which owns Bohemia Art, accused the liquidators of Kladno Holding of breaking the law.

- The Civic Democratic Alliance still insists on continuing deregulation and tax cutting even though it expects a serious conflict to arise soon within the coalition concerning the deregulation of energy prices and rents.

- President Vaclav Havel said that politicians are wrong in taking seriously the statements made by the Russian ambassador in Prague, who threatened economic sanctions by Moscow if the Czech Republic enters NATO.
